diagnoses.summary: High movement along normal correlations with large SPE indicates a coherent process upset with a dominant leakage in the reflux drum driving the disturbance.

PCA shows a coherent large upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The dominant contributor is the reflux drum level controller (DR_LIC) being saturated at a low PV relative to the setpoint, with drum holdup rising. Rule-based hints point to a DR_LIC-related issue, with reflux drum dynamics driving the major SPE contribution.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with strong hints of reflux drum issue and related control saturation. The most consistent fault is a reflux drum leak, with secondary contributions from condenser cooling issues and possible reboiler/leakage effects. The DR_LIC loop is saturated and driving abnormal valve/controller behavior, pointing downstream from the drum as the main source.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent movement (high T2) and significant SPE indicates a process upset with a dominant contributor at the reflux drum. The strongest evidence points to a leak in the reflux drum path, with the DR_LIC loop being highly influential and DR_LIC output saturated relative to setpoint.

A large, coherent upset centered on the reflux drum level control is driving a major shift in drum holdup and feeds. DR_LIC (drum level control) is saturated with PV off-set, indicating an actuator/level-control fault propagating through the reflux drum system. The reflux drum/leak pathways are consistent with the observed drum holdup rise and saturated control output.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by reflux drum/DR_LIC related signals and an actuator loop saturation. The strongest single rule-based hypothesis is DR_LIC_out_of_range (drum level controller output saturated while PV off setpoint).

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T² and SPE, with distillate acetone disturbance and elevated tray temperatures. Fault hypotheses from catalogue focus on condenser/columns control anomalies and reflux path issues, consistent with the active DIST_X_L alarm and saturated DR_LIC control.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T2 and SPE violations, driven by a dominant contribution from distillate-related measurements and distillate flow control. The fixed-rule evidence points to a condenser cooling efficiency issue causing abnormal column behavior and a distillate leak alarm (DIST_X_L).
Abnormal PCA with large, coherent upset dominated by distillate acetone deviation and condenser-related symptoms; most likely condenser cooling effectiveness loss affecting the distillation column.

A large, coherent process upset with strong SPE and high T², dominated by distillate acetone anomaly and column/condensation disturbances. The most likely fault is condenser cooling effectiveness loss causing poor condensation and abnormal distillate acetone signal; other plausible contributors include reflux flow issues and H2 PCV related constraints.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The most likely root cause is condenser cooling effectiveness loss affecting the distillation section, with several interlinked issues (H2 PCV/pressure probes and reflux dynamics) also plausible.
PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong distillate acetone signal and condenser-related indicators; most likely a condenser cooling issue causing loss of condenser effectiveness.
High coherence-dominated upset with a strong disturbance in the distillate acetone stream and a likely condenser cooling issue propagating through the column.

PCA shows a large coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The top contributing measurements point to abnormal distillate acetone composition and related column support links, with the strongest single signal coming from the distillate acetone composition alarm and related reflux/control signals. Rule evidence most strongly supports a condenser cooling effectiveness loss driving the disturbance.
